RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 55

An all-male panel is not definitive proof of discrimination, but homogeneous committees carry documented risks of in-group affinity and unconscious bias. This dynamic often leads evaluators to favor subjective attributes over formal credentials like your master's degree, professional licensure, and direct municipal experience.

Raising gender bias immediately in an informal follow-up, however, will likely provoke defensiveness and close doors. Instead, follow up politely on your requested debrief or request the interview scoring matrix via public records. Only raise the panel's gender composition as supporting context if you find documented procedural anomalies or decide to pursue a formal grievance through municipal HR, an ombudsperson, or legal counsel.
